title: What Happens If You Don't Brush Your Teeth for a Week?
sources: Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'How To Remove Plaque From Teeth' (RDH Tenika Patterson: plaque is 'soft and sticky at first, but if it's not removed within 24 hours, it hardens like cement. That's what we call tartar.'; 'Once plaque becomes tartar, only a dental professional can remove it'; 'Bacteria cause inflammation under your gum line'): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/how-to-remove-plaque-from-teeth

Cleveland Clinic, 'Plaque' (dental plaque is 'a sticky, colorless film of bacteria that forms on your teeth'; 'new plaque forms on your teeth every day and even at night while you sleep'; teeth that 'feel fuzzy' probably have plaque; tartar: 'Only a dentist or hygienist can remove it'): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/10953-plaque

Cleveland Clinic, 'Tartar' (tartar is hardened dental plaque; 'you can't remove tartar with brushing and flossing'; a dentist or dental hygienist must remove it; it can make gums swell and bleed): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/25102-tartar

Belstrom et al., 'Salivary cytokine levels in early gingival inflammation', Journal of Oral Microbiology 2017;9(1):1364101 (28 participants stopped brushing and interdental cleaning for 10 days: 'PI and GI values increased significantly during the experimental gingivitis period (at days, 4, 7, and 10)'; after resuming hygiene, 'After 2 weeks of resolution (day 24), PI and GI scores were not significantly different from baseline scores'): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5560406

NHS, 'Gum disease' (caused by a build-up of plaque; gums 'swollen, red and sore', bleeding when you brush; 'bad breath and a bad taste in your mouth'; see a dentist if your gums bleed when you brush): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/gum-disease/

Cleveland Clinic, 'Bad Breath (Halitosis)' ('The main cause of halitosis is poor oral hygiene'; 'Harmful bacteria invade your mouth and cause bad smells'): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/17771-bad-breath-halitosis

Tease (next video): Joly-Mascheroni, Senju & Shepherd, 'Dogs catch human yawns', Biology Letters 2008;4(5):446-448 (21 of 29 dogs yawned after watching a human yawn, none at control mouth movements; later studies replicated it only weakly, hence 'might'): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2610100

lines.text: What happens if you don't brush your teeth for a week?
lines.caps: WHAT *HAPPENS | IF YOU *DON'T | BRUSH YOUR *TEETH | FOR A *WEEK?

lines.text: Day eight, brush again. Gums heal in two weeks, or need a dentist?
lines.caps: DAY *EIGHT | BRUSH *AGAIN | GUMS *HEAL | IN TWO *WEEKS | OR *NEED | A *DENTIST?

lines.text: Day one: a sticky bacteria film coats them.
Ever woken up with fuzzy teeth? That's it.
But here's the twist: after a day, it hardens like cement.
lines.caps: BUT *HERE'S | THE *TWIST | AFTER A *DAY | IT *HARDENS | LIKE *CEMENT

lines.text: Day four: your gums are already inflamed.
Day seven: puffy gums, maybe bleeding, stinky breath.
Two weeks! One study: gums back to normal.
The cement? Only a dental pro.
